label: Original-phase input of j/0/f/n/r/h/e/u after an earlier v/3/l/d/m/i/x/p (weak, diffuse)
explanation: Mostly an original-phase unit (90% of activation mass during input of original tokens, 6% on <DEL>, 4% in the copy phase). Firing depends on the current input token: j has the highest rate (26%), then 0, f, n, r, h, e, u (10-15%). It also depends on what came earlier: sequences starting with or containing v, 3, l, d, m, i, x, p raise the rate. It mostly fires on the first occurrence of a token (86% of mass) and becomes more frequent late in long sequences (rate 30% at orig_idx 8, L=9 holds 37% of mass). The top activations are on the last one or two original tokens and on <DEL> in long sequences. It is rare in the copy phase, after recall_idx 0. Even the best predicate is weak (dev F1 about 0.39, precision 0.34, mass recall 0.59). The same inputs often fail to fire it, so it looks like a distributed function of the input token and the accumulated hidden state, not a clean feature.
